citations.F1: N+1 query in `serialize_event` — one `SELECT` per event against `users` (up to ~1900 sequential round trips for acme); batch-fetch actors with one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` query
citations.F2: dedupe uses `if key in seen` on a list (`seen: list[str]`), which is O(n²) over the event set; switch `seen` to a `set`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses a synchronous `requests.get` inside an async handler, blocking the entire worker's event loop for up to 2s per uncached IP; replace with an async HTTP client or run it in a thread pool
citations.F4: no index on `events(org_id, created_at)` — full scan of 4.2M rows every call; add a composite index `(org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` are module-level and never evicted or trimmed; ... cap or roll the timings list
citations.F6: each of 16 workers grows its own unbounded `_geo_cache` ... add a TTL/max-size cache for geo lookups
citations.F7: After 2–6, re-run the acme/northwind p50/p95 measurement (same Datadog query) before deciding whether any caching layer is still needed
citations.F8: Root cause of the 1.2–1.6s query: no index ... Root cause of the 6–12s wall time: N+1 query in `serialize_event`
citations.F9: Don't ship the on-call proposal as-is — it masks symptoms and the worker bump likely worsens the leak ... Only reconsider worker/pool sizing and a Redis response cache after the above land and are measured
